textbookText: 79. Which of the following correctly relates cohesive forces to a liquid's meniscus shape in a glass tube? A) If adhesive forces (liquid–glass) exceed cohesive forces, the liquid wets the glass forming a concave meniscus (e.g., water) B) If adhesive forces dominate, the meniscus is always convex C) Meniscus shape has nothing to do with intermolecular forces D) All liquids form identical meniscus shapes regardless of forces

80. Latent heat is absorbed/released during a change of state because it is used to: A) Overcome (or reform) intermolecular forces of attraction, not to change temperature B) Increase the average kinetic energy of the particles C) Increase the temperature of the substance D) Change the chemical identity of the substance

81. Mercury, unlike water, shows a convex meniscus in a glass tube because: A) Cohesive forces between mercury atoms exceed adhesive forces with glass B) Mercury has no surface tension C) Mercury evaporates faster than water D) Mercury is a solid at room temperature

82. The critical temperature of a gas is the temperature: A) Above which the gas cannot be liquefied no matter how much pressure is applied B) At which a gas always liquefies immediately C) Below absolute zero D) At which vapor pressure becomes exactly zero

83. Which of these processes releases heat to the surroundings (exothermic phase change)? A) Condensation (gas to liquid) B) Melting (solid to liquid) C) Vaporization (liquid to gas) D) Sublimation (solid to gas)

84. In liquid crystals (an intermediate/extraordinary state of matter used in LCD screens), molecules: A) Have some positional disorder like a liquid but retain a degree of directional order like a solid B) Are perfectly disordered, exactly like an ordinary gas C) Are perfectly ordered in three dimensions, exactly like a crystalline solid D) Have no intermolecular interactions at all

85. Which factor primarily determines whether a substance is solid, liquid, or gas at room temperature? A) The relative strength of intermolecular forces compared to thermal (kinetic) energy of particles B) The atomic number of the element only C) The color of the substance D) The electrical conductivity of the substance

86. Sublimation of solid carbon dioxide (dry ice) at room temperature and atmospheric pressure occurs because: A) Its triple point lies above atmospheric pressure, so it cannot exist as a liquid under normal atmospheric conditions B) It has an unusually high boiling point C) It has no intermolecular forces whatsoever D) It reacts chemically with air

87. Which of the following best describes the "triple point" of a substance? A) The unique temperature and pressure at which solid, liquid, and gas phases coexist in equilibrium B) The temperature at which a substance boils at any pressure C) The point where density of solid and gas become equal D) A point that exists only for water, not other substances

88. Compared to a solid, a liquid has: A) Greater freedom of molecular movement (particles can flow past one another) but still notable intermolecular attraction B) Completely free, independent molecular movement like a gas C) No molecular movement at all, being rigid D) Stronger intermolecular forces than in the solid state

89. Which everyday extraordinary fact illustrates sublimation? A) Naphthalene balls (mothballs) gradually disappear over time by turning directly into vapor B) Ice melting into water on a hot day C) Water boiling in a kettle D) Steam condensing on a cold window

90. Which of the following is TRUE regarding the density trend across states for most substances (excluding water)? A) Solid > Liquid > Gas, because particle packing is closest in solids and most spread out in gases B) Gas > Liquid > Solid always C) All three states have identical density D) Liquid is always denser than solid
